edges.description: The COG complex recycles Golgi glycosylation enzymes through retrograde intra-Golgi transport; when it fails, those enzymes are mislocalized.
Mislocalized Golgi enzymes leave glycoproteins underprocessed, losing terminal galactose and sialic acid on N-glycans and affecting O-glycans.
The combined N- and O-glycosylation defect is read out clinically as the type 2 serum transferrin and abnormal apolipoprotein C-III isoelectric focusing patterns.
Liver involvement is the most frequent COG6-CDG feature; the intermediate steps from hypoglycosylation to hepatopathy are not defined.
The authors hypothesise that severe COG6 loss impairs glycosylation of ADAM metalloproteases needed for gonadal distal tip cell migration; this route is untested.
COG deficiency is associated with recurrent febrile hyperinflammatory episodes; the authors suggest, but do not show, that the glycosylation defect drives the immune dysregulation.
In two of three reported COG6/COG7 patients, HLH episodes were followed by neurological deterioration and new-onset epilepsy.
The index patient had vitamin K deficiency together with intracranial bleeding; the abstract reports both without stating a causal link.
The 2015 review describes hypohidrosis as predisposing to hyperthermia.
